question_text: How many seats are on the Supreme Court?

why_it_matters.text: Nine justices share the work of the highest court — one Chief Justice and eight Associate Justices. Together they hear cases, debate the meaning of the law, and vote. An odd number means there's almost always a clear majority.

fun_fact.text: The Constitution doesn't set the size of the Supreme Court — Congress does! The Court has had 6, 7, 9, and even 10 justices over its history. It's been 9 since 1869. In 1937, President Franklin D. Roosevelt tried to expand it to 15 to win the rulings he wanted. Congress refused, and the number has stayed at 9 ever since.
